title: Greater Tokyo in 5 Days — Kawagoe, Atami Fireworks, Harajuku (Summer)
subtitle: Summer only: Kawagoe's Little Edo, the Atami fireworks and Harajuku, in and out of Narita
summary: Five summer days around Tokyo: the old streets of Kawagoe, the Atami sea fireworks, SHIBUYA SKY and Harajuku. The Atami fireworks only go off on set dates, so check the official site for the dates before you book flights. Tokyo Tower and other city sights are already in the Tokyo template, so they are not repeated here. Chiikawa ramen, the otter café and Yodobashi in Ueno sit in the alternates.

Could not be confirmed from official sources, so check before you go
The opening hours and closed days of each restaurant, the shopping malls, the former Hachijūgo Bank Head Office Main Building, Sunshine City, Tokyu Plaza Omotesando Harajuku and others.
The Kawagoe bus fares and timetables, and the coordinates for each spot, are estimates.
What changed and what was cut
On day 1 of the travelogue, SHIBUYA SKY and dinner are kept. The travelogue only passed Tokyo Tower, so it is not scheduled (template 02 already covers it).

The Chiikawa café, Chiikawa ramen, Chiikawa Park, rice crackers and sweet potato sticks on days 2, 3 and 5 of the travelogue are cut down to Ikebukuro's beef tongue and the Gashapon department store. Chiikawa ramen goes to the alternates.
Yodobashi in Ueno on day 5 of the travelogue is folded into the Ueno Marui stop and mentioned briefly.
Private shopping on day 4 of the travelogue, such as drugstore buys, perfume and bakery gifts, is left out.
Prerequisite: fit your dates to the Atami fireworks
The point of this trip is the Atami Sea Fireworks Festival (熱海海上花火大会) on day 3. It only goes off on set dates, so fix the date first and then plan the whole trip around it.
Check the dates on the Atami Tourist Association site: https://www.ataminews.gr.jp/event/8 . Do not assume a date, and do not work it out from dates of a past year.
Start times change with the season: the travelogue says about 20:15 in July and August and about 20:20 in other months, for about 20–25 min. Go by the official site.
The template is based on a summer travelogue from mid-September, so weather and daylight vary by season.
Getting between the airport and the city (Narita International Airport NRT)

Keisei Skyliner: Narita Terminal 2 to Keisei Ueno takes about 41 min, all seats reserved with no unreserved cars, about ¥2,580 (¥1,280 fare plus ¥1,300 reserved-seat fee, from the Keisei FAQ). The official Keisei Ueno page lists ¥2,470, which does not match, so check the Keisei site before you go.
The Keisei Main Line (Limited Express, Rapid or Access Express) is cheaper but slower. Check the Keisei site for timetables and fares.
The JR Narita Express goes direct to Tokyo Station, Shinagawa, Shinjuku and Ikebukuro. Check the JR East site for timetables and fares.

The travelogue took the Skyliner to Keisei Ueno and changed to the Ginza Line for Shimbashi. After immigration, follow the signs for the railway to the SKYLINER & KEISEI INFORMATION CENTER to exchange your ticket, and note that other railways have their own counters.

This template picks Narita because the travelogue flew in and out of Narita and the Skyliner is fastest to Ueno. You could use Haneda instead; look up the Keikyu line or the Tokyo Monorail separately.
Transport tickets
For a transit card use Suica, including Suica in an iPhone. The airport stations have machines for Welcome Suica and regular Suica top-ups.

Kawagoe Discount Pass (train plus Tobu Bus): round trip on the Tobu Tojo Line from Ikebukuro to Kawagoe, plus all-day Tobu Bus (including the Tobu Koedo loop bus). There are two bus companies, Seibu and Tobu, and this pass only covers Tobu. Do not tap Suica when you use the pass.
Seibu's "Koedo Loop Bus" does not accept the Tobu pass. You can pay with a transit card or buy Seibu's own pass.

The Tōkaidō Shinkansen between Tokyo and Atami is run by JR Central and JR West, and you can book early online. The travelogue bought tickets about 4 weeks before travel (2025 data) and went through the gates with the e-ticket QR code.
Reservations and tickets

SHIBUYA SKY: the official site https://www.shibuya-scramble-square.com/sky/ is very popular, so buy early. The travelogue bought the 18:40 night slot. You must store your selfie stick before entering, and there are free lockers upstairs.
teamLab Borderless: official site https://www.teamlab.art/e/borderless-azabudai/ . Buying ahead is recommended. There is no map inside, but there is an official leaflet at the entrance.

Chiikawa Mogumogu Honpo Kawagoe: entry is limited all day. You can scan the QR code on site to reserve the next slot, or reserve online to be safe. One phone and one account can reserve only once a day.

HARRY Harajuku terrace otter café: reserve on the official site https://harinezumi-cafe.com/store/harajuku-terrace/ . Reservations are at least 60 min, and going on the day may leave you empty-handed.
Atami: the beach is free and has no paid seating, so bring your own picnic mat. Buy the return Shinkansen ahead, because the station is crowded after the fireworks.
Entry
You can enter without a visa. Register on Visit Japan Web before you arrive. The immigration and customs QR codes are now combined (from the 2025 travelogue; check the Visit Japan Web site).
Pacing

Days 1 and 5 include the airport, day 2 is a round trip to Kawagoe and day 3 a round trip to Atami, so there is a lot of travel. On day 3 you are back at the hotel around 22:45 after the fireworks, later than 21:00.
You stay 4 nights in a row at Daiwa Roynet Hotel Tokyo Shimbashi, about 2 min on foot from Shimbashi Station. The rooms are on the small side.

notes.title: Trip overview: how the 5 days run
paragraphs: In and out of Narita Terminal 2, with one hotel in Shimbashi as the base for all four nights, plus a day trip to Kawagoe and another to Atami, both by train and back the same day. The heart of this trip is the Atami Sea Fireworks Festival on day 3. The fireworks run only on set dates, so confirm the date first and then plan the whole trip around it.
Day 1: land at Narita, drop your bags in Shimbashi, then go to Shibuya for the night view from {@d1-03} and kushikatsu for dinner at the Shibuya PARCO food hall.

Day 2: Kawagoe for {@d2-01}, then the Chiikawa Mogumogu Honpo Kawagoe branch for its Kawagoe-only sweet potato items, lunch at the second-floor café of the former Hachijūgo Bank main building, and an afternoon along {@d2-04}; back in Ikebukuro for beef tongue and the capsule toy store at Sunshine City.

Day 3: Kobe beef for lunch at Tokyo Station and the character shops on Ichibangai, then the train to Atami for a stock-up on the shopping street by the station and at a convenience store; in the evening settle in at {@d3-04} and wait for {@d3-05}, getting back to the hotel around 22:45.

Day 4: {@d4-01} at Azabudai Hills in the morning with a fruit mille-feuille at HARBS for lunch; in the afternoon Harajuku for Tokyu Plaza and KIDDY LAND, wagyu sliders, then {@d4-05}, and Imari beef steak for dinner at Shibuya PARCO.
Day 5: {@d5-01} in Ueno, lunch near Ueno Station, collect your bags and buy gifts at {@d5-03}, then Narita Terminal 2 for duty-free shopping before you depart.
Where to sleep: Daiwa Roynet Hotel Tokyo Shimbashi for all four nights, about a 2-minute walk from Shimbashi Station; the rooms are small.

Getting around: from Narita Terminal 2 to Keisei Ueno take the Keisei Skyliner, about 41 minutes, all reserved seats, with the fare on the Keisei website; Ikebukuro to Kawagoe is about 30 minutes on the Tobu Tojo Line, and the Kawagoe pass covers Tobu buses only; Tokyo to Atami is the Tokaido Shinkansen, which you can book online ahead; Suica works as your transit card. Check the fireworks date on the Atami tourism association website and never assume one. Check the latest timetables before you go.

Who it suits: anyone who wants Kawagoe, the Atami fireworks, Harajuku and Chiikawa spots in a single trip. Days 2 and 3 are Kawagoe and Atami round trips, so travel time is heavy, and you get back to the hotel late on fireworks night; confirm the fireworks date before you book flights and hotel.
